detail.longDescription: I have written a shell script which issues commands to build a Rust --bin project and to install that built binary to /usr/local/bin/ or some/other/standard/bin/location depending on the target OS. I would like to use the same script for different target OS'es. When it's built for linux the location of built binary is ${WORKSPACE_DIR}/target/release , but when I build it for vxworks the location is ${WORKSPACE_DIR}/target/aarch64-wrs-vxworks/release . So, in order to make this installation OS agnostic, is there a way to know or some cargo environment variable that contains the built binary path that I can use for installation. when compiled for VxWorks install -Dm 755 ${WORKSPACE_DIR}/target/${TARGET_ARCH}/${PROFILE}/${PACKAGE_NAME}.vxe ${INSTALL_PREFIX_PATH}/bin/${PACKAGE_NAME} When compiled for Linux install -Dm 755 ${WORKSPACE_DIR}/target/${PROFILE}/${PACKAGE_NAME}.vxe ${INSTALL_PREFIX_PATH}/bin/${PACKAGE_NAME} Expected script code install -Dm 755 ${TARGET_DIR_LOCATION}/${PACKAGE_NAME}.vxe ${INSTALL_PREFIX_PATH}/bin/${PACKAGE_NAME}
